data.title: Otis Worldwide Announces CEO Succession and Leadership Transition
data.description:
Otis Worldwide ( (OTIS) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On September 15, 2026, Otis Worldwide announced that Chair, Chief Executive Officer and President Judy Marks will retire upon the appointment of her successor, expected in the first half of 2027, or by July 31, 2027 at the latest. She will also step down from the Board on the transition date and may serve as a non-employee senior advisor through July 31, 2027 to support a smooth leadership handover.

The Board has activated its long-standing CEO succession plan, forming an independent succession committee led by Christopher J. Kearney and engaging Spencer Stuart to run a comprehensive search across internal and external candidates. The orderly transition underscores Otis’s confidence in its value-creation strategy, which under Marks has delivered strong free cash flow, expanded its high-margin service portfolio to about 2.5 million units, and returned $8.4 billion to shareholders, reinforcing the company’s positioning as a leading urban mobility player.

data.title: Coya Therapeutics Advances COYA 302 ALS Phase 2/3 Trial
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Coya Therapeutics, Inc. ( (COYA) ).

On September 15, 2026, Coya Therapeutics reported that the one hundredth patient has been enrolled in its ongoing Phase 2/3 ALSTARS Trial of COYA 302 for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. The randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled study aims to enroll 120 participants, with current trends supporting completion in time to report topline data in early Q2 2027.

The trial is structured with a 24-week double-blind treatment phase followed by a 24-week blinded active-treatment extension, giving up to 48 weeks of data on COYA 302. Its primary endpoint is change in disease severity measured by ALSFRS-R from baseline to Week 24 versus placebo, with additional objectives focused on efficacy, safety, tolerability, biological activity, and biomarker assessments, underscoring Coya’s push to advance its ALS program.
